subject: Celestia Finance — DR / RTO-RPO clarifications for resilience section of RFP

Subject: RFP - resilience appendix clarifications (RTO / RPO and failover sequencing)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the earlier materials; our evaluation team is working through the resilience section and has asked for a few clarifications so we can score Redwood consistently against other vendors. High-level asks:

- For your hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment options, can you confirm the practical RTO and RPO targets you design for in customers' PROD SLAs (e.g., "RTO 10 min / RPO 1 min" vs "RTO 2 hours / RPO 0"). Please call out any dependencies (model size, region, sync vs async replication).
- Describe the multi-region failover sequencing: what is warm-standby vs active-active for Redwood, and what steps are automated vs operator-driven?
- How do you handle in-flight requests and model KV cache state during failover?
- We also need evidence of recent DR rehearsals (summary acceptable) and runbook snippets showing cutover steps.

Procurement has included these as part of the resilience scoring; if possible, please provide a short written response and any attachments we can include in the RFP package. We may ask for a 60-minute technical call after reviewing.

Thanks,
Jordan Price
Sr. Infrastructure Architect
Celestia Finance

Subject: Re: RFP - resilience appendix clarifications (RTO / RPO and failover sequencing)

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise set of answers up front; I attached a short DR appendix (+test summary and runbook snippets) for your RFP pack. Happy to do a deep-dive call.

Executive summary (by deployment mode):

- Hosted API (Redwood-managed multi-tenant):
  - Typical operational target: RTO 5–30 minutes (depends on model warm/cold state and region propagation).
  - RPO target: near-zero for model artifacts (cross-region object replication), 30–120 seconds for ephemeral session metadata when using our optional prefix caching replication.
  - Failover mode: automated regional routing + active-passive request spillover. If a region reports unhealthy, traffic is shifted to healthy regions via routing policy; model warm-up may be required for large quantized models.

- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in customer tenant):
  - Operational target with warm-standby configured: RTO 5–15 minutes for API-level recovery; RPO < 60 seconds for control-plane metadata when synchronous replication is enabled; near-zero for model artifacts if S3 cross-region replication is configured during onboarding.
  - If Dedicated is configured in active-active across two regions, RTO degrades to sub-minute for routing-level failover but requires customer acceptance of eventual consistency for ephemeral caches.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Targets vary by customer topology; typical commitments we support in Private engagements: RTO 15–60 minutes (fully operator-driven cutover without dedicated cross-region automation), RPO depends on storage replication method — from near-zero (block-level sync) to minutes (async object replication).

Key dependencies and notes:
- Model size & cache state: very large models (30B+) and quantized weights increase cold-starts; we proactively stage model shards to standby nodes when warm-standby is requested to meet sub-15 minute RTOs.
- Storage replication: model binaries are stored in object stores with optional cross-region replication; control-plane metadata can be configured for synchronous replication for Dedicated customers needing stricter RPOs.
- KV / prefix cache: we offer both local in-memory caches and an optional replicated prefix/KV cache. When the optional replicated cache is enabled, we aim for RPO < 60s; otherwise, on failover cache is rebuilt (in-flight inference may re-run).

Failover sequencing (high-level automated vs manual):
1) Detection & routing: health checks detect region/unhealthy pools and initiate routing changes (automated).
2) Model availability: if the target region has model on warm-standby, traffic switches promptly; otherwise automatic background model pull is initiated (automated, but warm-up time applies).
3) Request handling & in-flight requests: active requests are retried via client SDK policies. In-flight state is best-effort unless you enable our replicated session store.
4) Operator verification & rollback: runbook contains verification gates and rollback steps (operator-driven).

Evidence & rehearsals: attached is a one-page DR test summary (Redwood internal March 2028 warm-standby exercise) and runbook_snippets.txt with the cutover checklist we provide customers.

Attachments included: Redwood_DR_Appendix_v2.pdf, DR_Test_Summary_Celestia_2028-03.xlsx, runbook_snippets.txt

Next step — would a 60-minute technical review with our SRE + Solutions Engineering team work for Thursday 19 Apr? If you have hard SLA targets you want to propose (e.g., firm RTO 10 minutes for Dedicated), list them and we will map them to our configuration options and proof points.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: internal: Celestia RFP - a few tactical clarifications for the runbook

Team — Jordan asked good questions. Two tactical clarifications we should surface back in the appendix and in the call:

1) KV cache expiration & failback: add explicit note that during failback we perform cache invalidation windows (configurable 0–300s) to avoid serving stale context; customers who need continuous session semantics should opt into the replicated session store.

2) Canary / phased traffic shift: recommend we propose a canary plan (10% -> 50% -> 100% over 5–15 min) in the RFP answer to show controlled risk. Include the rollback trigger thresholds (error rate delta, tail latency spike, 5xx > 1% sustained).

3) Data sovereignty: call out that for Dedicated and Private deployments, cross-region replication is configurable per customer and we document region pairings in onboarding (important for Celestia compliance).

I'll prep a 2-slide summary for the call highlighting these three points and the RTO/RPO table Marissa provided.

-Ben
Sr. Product Manager, Reliability

Subject: Re: RFP - resilience appendix clarifications (RTO / RPO and failover sequencing)

Marissa,

Appreciate the detailed response and the attachments — that’s helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we land the scorecard:

- For Dedicated with warm-standby, can you commit to an operational RTO of 10 minutes as a target bound we can score? We understand warm-standby requires model staging but our risk committee wants a bounded expectation.
- For the replicated session store, is the replication synchronous by default or an opt-in feature? We need to understand whether enabling it will incur latency impact.
- Please include the March 2028 test summary as evidence in the RFP package (we will include it in our appendix).

Can we take the technical call Friday 20 Apr at 14:00 PT? That should fit our eval team's calendar.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: Re: RFP - resilience appendix clarifications (RTO / RPO and failover sequencing)

Jordan — confirmed for Fri 20 Apr at 14:00 PT (we'll send a calendar invite). Quick answers in advance so your committee has language: 

- Dedicated warm-standby target: we can commit to an operational target of RTO 10 minutes for Dedicated when warm-standby is configured and model staging is completed during onboarding. We will include the configuration checklist and acceptance criteria in the appendix.
- Replicated session store: opt-in feature. It is configurable as synchronous replication for control-plane/session metadata (adds ~5–12ms median write latency depending on region pair); we document the impact and provide performance knobs.

Agenda for the 60-minute call (we will send slides):
  1) Quick summary of RTO/RPO by deployment mode (10m)
  2) Warm-standby design and model staging (15m)
  3) Replicated session store and cache strategies (10m)
  4) DR test summary & evidence walkthrough (10m)
  5) Q&A and next steps (15m)

Attachments reiterated: Redwood_DR_Appendix_v2.pdf, DR_Test_Summary_Celestia_2028-03.xlsx, runbook_snippets.txt

See you on the call. If procurement needs a formal signed addendum for the RTO commitment, let us know and we will loop Legal/Sales.

Best regards,
Marissa
